thread_analysis.thread_summary: Key System (relayed via Masaya Iida, original inquiry details unspecified contact) requests Bluetooth SIG certification quotes for two products: a smart jump rope (BLE, Core Spec 4.2, no already-certified chip used) and a smart band (BLE, Core Spec 6, Nordic nRF54L15 module, external monopole antenna). Itsuo Sakai provides scoping explanations and quotes for each.
all_questions_found: What test scope applies to a product not implementing an already-certified SoC? (see thread_0284_case_01)

(Administrative, standard quote) Cost estimate for the smart band using the already-registered Nordic nRF54L15 module: RF PHY test, profile test (DIS, BAS), registration support, Compliance Folder creation.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The two products illustrate a direct contrast: the smart jump rope (no certified chip) faces the full middle-protocol-layer testing burden, while the smart band (already-certified Nordic nRF54L15 module) only needs RF PHY and profile-layer testing, demonstrating concretely why component choice drives certification scope and cost.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When quoting for multiple products in one inquiry, use a contrasting pair (certified vs. uncertified component) as a teaching opportunity to make the cost/scope impact of component choice concrete for the customer.
